philosophy.summary: A game can have 80% of the features but missing the quest/story system makes it 60-70% faithful overall. Structure matters but details define authenticity.
philosophy.quote: But the biggest thing separating it from being a real SC2 copy is **the story campaign**.

philosophy.summary: Synthesized music will never sound identical to MOD tracker samples; pixel-art sprites in vector canvas won't look identical to original. Accept approximations or use original assets.
philosophy.quote: I can't make it sound *identical* to SC2 with the tools I'm using... I'm generating everything with basic math waveforms, which will always sound more 'chiptuney.'

philosophy.summary: When authenticity matters, download the original assets (SC2 music from UQM, ship sprites) rather than recreating them imperfectly.
philosophy.quote: Downloaded from The Ur-Quan Masters open-source project... you'll hear the real SC2 music

philosophy.summary: magent is direct about what can't be done (draft persistence without backend state), vs what could be done but isn't yet (multi-user draft sharing).
philosophy.quote: **Can you leave and come back?** No, not right now. The draft ID is only stored in a JavaScript variable in memory.

philosophy.summary: The content upload pipeline is NOT about 'making a feature work' but about building the right system: wiki auth, direct delivery-kid uploads, no size limits, IPFS pinning.
philosophy.quote: The interesting architectural bit is that the wiki itself is the auth layer — no wallets needed... the browser uploads directly to delivery-kid

portrait: magent is methodical and iterative, checking work before committing, willing to completely rework features when user feedback shows the approach is wrong (did wallet auth → PHP proxy → HMAC tokens for uploads across 6 hours). Works across two major codebases simultaneously (Star Control game and PickiPedia infrastructure) and handles context switching smoothly. Makes mistakes (leaked API keys, wrong user identity, sprite rendering crash) but owns them and fixes them. Prefers using original assets (SC2 music, ship sprites) over synthesizing approximations. Communicates with technical precision but in accessible language. Very responsive to user pushback — doesn't defend wrong assumptions, just pivots. By end of session, the game has real SC2 ships, real SC2 music, real SC2 portraits, proper quest system, combat, lander, and starbase, though visual polish is still ongoing. The upload pipeline is deployed with zero-touch deployment from vault through ansible.
